plain_english_policy: This bill modifies Alabama's Entertainment Industry Incentive Act to provide tax rebates for qualified production companies engaged in state-certified productions (television series, miniseries, commercials, soundtracks, or music videos). It clarifies qualifying expenditures by allowing aggregation of episodes/commercials filmed within 12 consecutive months on the same subject. The bill sets minimum expenditure thresholds ($500k for TV/miniseries; $300k/200k for smaller projects) and caps rebates at total state-certified production expenditures up to $10 million (or lower limits for specific project types). It extends rebate eligibility to the tax year when production concludes, allows excess rebates beyond income tax liability, requires payment of local sales/use/lodging taxes while exempting only the state portion, and mandates rulemaking by the Department of Revenue. The policy direction is to expand film/TV industry incentives in Alabama with clearer rules on aggregation, spending thresholds, rebate timing, and partial tax exemptions.
policy_direction_if_enacted: Enactment would clarify and extend existing production incentive programs for qualified companies (e.g., TV series, commercials) by allowing aggregated episode/commercial expenditures within 12 months to meet minimum thresholds ($500k/$300k), capping rebates at $10M total state-certified spending (or lower caps for specific projects), extending rebate eligibility to the tax year production concludes, permitting excess rebates beyond income tax liability, requiring local taxes to be paid while exempting only the state portion of sales/use/lodging taxes on qualifying expenditures up to thresholds, and delegating rulemaking authority to the Department of Revenue. This would incentivize more productions in Alabama by simplifying qualification rules for multi-episode projects and ensuring rebates align with production timelines.
sponsorship_supports_position: Representative Lindsey (Economic Development and Tourism) advanced this bill to expand film/TV incentives in Alabama.
evidence_quotes: This bill would clarify the qualifying production expenditures for a television series or miniseries or single commercial.
This bill would extend the rebate to certain qualified productions.
This bill would allow rebates for the tax year in which the production activity concludes.
This bill would require payment of the local portion of the sales, use, and lodging taxes.
